simple.meaning: גּוּד (gûwd) is a Hebrew word meaning “to crowd upon , i.e. attack.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: גּוּד (H1464) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 49:19, with occurrences in Genesis, Habakkuk.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גּוּד (H1464) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גּוּד (H1464) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גּוּד (gûwd) / H1464 is traced through Genesis 49:19, Habakkuk 3:16 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1464. gud [ גּוּד ] verb invade, attack (compare גדד , whence יָגֻד etc. actually derived by Ki Bö Kö i. 356 q. v.; SS, perhaps better, denominative from גדוד ) — Qal Imperfect יָגֻד Gen 49:19 , יְגוּדֶ֑נּוּ 49:19 , יְגֻדֶנּ֑וּ Hab 3:16 ; יגודו Psa 94:21 Kt (see גדד ); — attack Gen 49:19 , alliteration with גָּד proper name & ׃ עֵָקב יָגֻד וְהוּא יְגוּדֶנּ֑וּ גְּדוּד גָּד גְּדוּד, Gad, a troop shall troop upon him, but he shall troop upon the heel (i.e. pursue them in their retreat) VB; Hab 3:16 יְגֻדֶ֑נּוּ לְעַם לַעֲלוֺת compare VB & Comm.
